newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends weaker on stocks rise but off lows.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends weaker on stocks rise but off lows.

text.p: Copper dipped lower in volatile trading on Friday following a rise in London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks, but prices ended off lows.
Three-months copper finished the day at $2,242, off $13 from Thursday's kerb close, after bouncing off support around $2,220 in the afternoon ring, analysts said.
A moderate rise in LME stocks, the first since early September, had pushed prices lower on profit-taking and general liquidation, dealers said.

But losses were kept to a minimum as the market was nervous about the upcoming December options declaration. The main concern was if December copper got close to $2,600 where there was a large concentration of open interest on calls.

"The stocks kept copper on the back foot for most of the day. But we've not seen a lot of weakness simply because of the options declaration on Wedensday," said analyst Robin Bhar of brokers Brandeis.
The nearby backwardation was still wide despite the stock increase, which deterred more aggressive selling, Bhar said.
Earlier nearby spreads showed a tendency to narrow, although late flurries of borrowing ensured that they closed little changed. The cash to threes backwardation was around $245.
Aluminium traded in a tight range for most of the day after slipping lower in early trading despite a decline in LME stocks.
It finished near its lows at $1,529.50 per tonne, versus $1,555 on Thursday.
"It could have fallen further but forward interest helped underpin it," one dealer said.
In the near term aluminium was expected to consolidate and attempt to form a base after rallying to 6-month highs earlier this week, analysts said.
Lead prices trundled to 10-month lows early and ended the kerb at $686, down $8.
A sizeable stocks rise after a large shipment into the Singapore warehouse coupled with weakening technicals painted a weak picture overall for lead, analysts said.
Zinc finished $3 firmer at $1,069 after a 4,925 stocks fall while tin edged up $30 to $6,110.
Nickel dropped $100 to $6,820 per tonne, following a stock rise of 630 tonnes.
"It's meeting pretty steady selling into any attempts to rally from here," Bhar said.
